title: Labels, legends, titles that make a claim, and annotations

videos.script: Most charts in a report have a title like this one. Monthly orders by region, twenty twenty-four to twenty twenty-five. {{label}} It is accurate, and it tells the reader nothing they could not see. They still have to find the point themselves, and two readers may find two different ones. {{nothing}} Now give the same chart this title. Northeast overtook South in October twenty twenty-four, and kept pulling away. {{claim}} The chart has not changed. But it has stopped being a picture to explore, and become evidence for a sentence. The reader checks the claim against the lines in two seconds, and agrees or does not. {{evidence}} Titles are one of four kinds of text on a chart. The others are labels, legends and annotations. Each one either saves the reader work or makes them do it. {{four}} This lesson is about writing all four, and about the numbers that sit on a chart. {{plan}}
